Safety

# Meet people the smart way.

2NIGHT is built for spontaneous, real-life nights. A few simple habits keep them fun — and keep you in control when you meet someone new.

01
### Meet in a public place
For a first meet, pick somewhere busy and well-lit. Stay in public until you genuinely feel comfortable.

02
### Tell a friend your plans
Let someone you trust know where you're going, who you're meeting, and when you'll be back.

03
### Never send money
Never send money, gift cards, or crypto to someone you met on the app, no matter the story.

04
### Trust your gut
If something feels off, it probably is. End the chat, leave the meet — there's no wrong reason to walk away.

05
### Report & block
Anyone who makes you uncomfortable can be blocked and reported in a tap. Flagging keeps the night safer for everyone.

06
### You're in control
You decide when you're live, how far your radius reaches, and what you share. We don't run background checks, so your own judgement comes first.

## Why same-night meetings need their own habits

2NIGHT is a one-night dating app for iPhone that shows who is out near you tonight, so you can match and meet the same evening instead of chatting for days. That speed is the point, and it also means you will often meet someone you first saw an hour ago. The six habits above are not a lecture; they are the short list that keeps a quick plan a good one. Two of them deserve a longer explanation.

Meet in public, every first time. A first meet is a bar, a café, a venue or a busy square — never a private home, never a car, never an isolated spot, whatever the story. If a plan on 2NIGHT names a private address as the venue, treat that as a reason to skip it.

Keep your own way home. Know your route, keep enough battery and cash for a taxi, and do not rely on the person you just met for a ride. Being able to leave at any moment is what makes trusting your gut possible.

## The tools inside the app

Two-minute video call. From any match you can start a short video or voice call. It runs peer-to-peer between the two phones (it never passes through our servers) and it is the quickest honest check that a person is who their photos say. It is free for everyone during the launch period. As on any peer-to-peer call, each side can technically see the other's IP address.

Hide me. One tap takes you out of every feed immediately. A “Tonight” status also expires by itself at 5 AM, so you never stay visible by accident.

Rounded distances only. Other members receive your distance in whole kilometres from the server, never your coordinates. If you do not go live for about 30 days, your stored position is blurred to your city.

Block. From a profile or the ⋯ menu in a chat. A block is instant, silent and works both ways: you disappear from each other's Tonight feed, pings stop, shared plans drop one of you, and the conversation leaves both inboxes. Nobody is told. You can undo a block under Settings → Safety & privacy.

Report. Tap the shield on a profile, or Report in the ⋯ menu of a chat, and choose one of three reasons: inappropriate content, fake or scam, or harassment. Reports are confidential by design — no member, including the person who filed it, can read a report back — and a person reviews every one, usually within 24 hours and always within 72. The outcome is removal, a warning, or closure; a closed report is never held against you. If a report describes a credible threat, we pass it to law enforcement. Details, including appeals and how long reports are kept, are on the Guidelines page.

Contact details stay in the app until you choose. Free members cannot send phone numbers, social handles, emails or links in chat. That rule exists for membership reasons, but it has a useful side effect: you can agree on a bar and a time without handing over your number to someone you have not met.

## What 2NIGHT does not do

We do not run background checks or identity checks, and there is no verification badge. Nobody at 2NIGHT reads your chats, and the app does not scan messages for abusive language — the only automatic checks are a short list of prohibited terms when you save your bio, and the contact-details rule above. That is why reporting matters so much: a word list cannot tell that someone made you uncomfortable, but you can.

## Scams, in one paragraph

Never send money, gift cards or cryptocurrency to anyone you met in the app, no matter how good the reason sounds — a stranded traveller, a medical bill, an investment tip, a “verification fee”. 2NIGHT never asks for payment outside the App Store, and a real match does not need your money to have a drink with you. Report the account with “fake or scam” and block it.

## If something goes wrong

If you are in danger, contact local emergency services first — they can reach you in minutes; we are one person reading a queue. Then report the account so we can act on it. If a report or a block decision looks wrong to you, email safety@2night.co from the address on your account and a person will look again. Removals and warnings are made by people, and people can be wrong; if we were, we reverse it.

## In an emergency, call for help.

If you ever feel unsafe, contact your local emergency services first. To report someone to us, email our team — we read every message.

Trust & Security

# Your safety, by design.

Meeting new people should feel exciting, not risky. Here's how 2NIGHT protects you and your data.

01
### You're always in control
You decide when you're live, how far your radius reaches, and what you share. Go offline and you disappear.

02
### Private by default
Only people inside the radius and audience you choose can see you, and only while you're live.

03
### Your data, protected
Encrypted in transit, access strictly limited, and never sold. Read the details in our Privacy Policy.

04
### Block & report in a tap
Anyone who makes you uncomfortable can be blocked and reported instantly. Our team reviews every report.

## Where your data lives

2NIGHT is a one-night dating app for iPhone that shows who is out near you tonight, so you can match and meet the same evening instead of chatting for days. Almost everything you put into it — account, status, photos, plans, messages — is stored in Supabase, our database, authentication and file-storage provider, processed primarily within the European Union. Apple handles Sign in with Apple, subscription billing and push notifications; a push says that something happened and who it involves, never the contents of a message. The complete list of providers, with what each one sees, is in the Privacy Policy .

There is no analytics, advertising, attribution or crash-reporting service in the app. There is no tracking SDK. We do not sell personal data and we do not share it for behavioural advertising.

## Location

Your location is read at roughly kilometre accuracy, only while you are live, and only to centre the Tonight Feed and rank people by distance. Other members receive a rounded distance in kilometres from the server; your coordinates are never sent to anyone. If you have not gone live for about 30 days, a routine on our database snaps your stored position to the centre of your city. Going offline in the app, or turning location off in iOS settings, stops sharing immediately.

## Who you want to see

Choosing to see women, men or non-binary people can reveal your sexual orientation, which the GDPR treats as special-category data. So 2NIGHT stores that choice only if you tick a separate, explicit consent box; choosing “Everyone” stores nothing. The choice is never shown to any member and is deleted the moment you withdraw consent, from Settings → Tonight → Who you see. Declining costs you nothing: your feed is not restricted and you are not hidden.

## Chats and calls

Nobody at 2NIGHT reads your messages, and the app does not scan them for abusive language. The one automatic check on messages looks for phone numbers, social handles, emails and links — a membership rule about when contact details can be exchanged, not a safety filter. Messages are kept while your account exists and deleted with it, immediately. Video and voice calls run peer-to-peer over WebRTC directly between the two phones; we never hold the call. Your device asks a Google STUN server how it is reachable (Google sees your IP address in that step), and, as on any peer-to-peer call, the other person can see your IP address and you can see theirs.

## Reports are confidential by design

When you report someone, the report lands in a queue only our safety reviewer can read. No member can read a report — including the person who wrote it — which is enforced in the database, not just promised here: if you could read your own report, someone who harasses several people could work out which of them filed. The person you report is never told who did, and never sees that a report exists until something happens to their account. Reports closed without action are deleted after 90 days; acted-on reports lose their evidence after 12 months and are deleted after 24. Blocks are equally quiet: nobody is told they have been blocked.

## Your rights and controls

From Settings you can export a copy of your data (the export is produced by a function that can only ever return the caller's own data) and delete your account. Deletion removes your profile, photos and messages; reports other people filed about you stay for the periods above, so a record cannot be wiped by deleting and re-registering. You can withdraw location consent, withdraw the “who you want to see” consent, and unblock anyone you have blocked, all from inside the app. For anything else, email support@2night.co; EEA and UK users can also complain to the CNIL, the French data protection authority.

## What we do not claim

We do not verify identities, photos or ages beyond the age you declare (the selector starts at 18). We do not run background checks and there is no verification badge. The two-minute video call, meeting in public and telling a friend are the honest substitutes, and our Safety page explains how to use them.

Important: 2NIGHT does not run background or identity checks. Meet in public, tell a friend, and trust your gut — see our Safety tips.

Questions about security or privacy? Email support@2night.co.

Community

# Community Guidelines

2NIGHT only works if it feels safe and real. These rules keep the night good for everyone — break them and you're out.

01
### Be real
Use your own photos and real details. No fake profiles, impersonation, or catfishing.

02
### Be respectful
No harassment, hate, threats, or unsolicited explicit content. Treat people the way you'd want to be treated.

03
### 18 and over only
2NIGHT is strictly for adults. Anyone underage is removed immediately.

04
### No money, no business
No selling, escorting, soliciting, scams, or asking members for money, gifts, or crypto.

05
### Keep it consensual
No recording or sharing anyone without consent, no doxxing, no sharing private information.

06
### Report what's wrong
Block and report anyone who crosses a line. Our team reviews every report — flagging keeps the night safe.

Read the full rules — how to report, how to block, and what we do about it →

## Why the rules are short

2NIGHT is a one-night dating app for iPhone that shows who is out near you tonight, so you can match and meet the same evening instead of chatting for days. It puts strangers in the same bar on a few hours' notice. That only works if everyone can trust that the person in the feed is real, is an adult, and will take a “no” as an answer. Six rules cover that; the rest is enforcement, and enforcement is what this page is mostly about.

## What is checked automatically — and what is not

When you save your bio (150 characters at most) it is checked against a short list of prohibited terms and refused if it matches. That is the only automatic content check on profiles, and it is deliberately narrow: it catches the worst slurs and will not catch anything clever. Messages are not read by anyone at 2NIGHT and are not scanned for abuse. The one check on messages looks for phone numbers, social handles, emails and links; it is a membership rule about when contact details can be exchanged, not a safety filter.

Which is why the sixth rule is the important one. A word list cannot tell that someone made you uncomfortable. You can, in two taps.

## How reporting works

Open a profile and tap the shield, or open the ⋯ menu at the top of a chat and choose Report. Pick one of three reasons — inappropriate content, fake or scam, or harassment — and it is sent. Your report goes into a queue that only our safety reviewer can read; no member, including you, can read it back, and the person you reported is never told who filed. We read the queue every day, aim to act within 24 hours and always act within 72. The outcome is one of three: the account is removed (it disappears from the feed, likes and plans, is signed out and can no longer message or ping anyone), the account is warned (the report stays on its record), or the report is closed because nothing was broken. A closed report is never held against you; we would rather you over-report than sit on something.

If you think we got a decision wrong — a removal or a warning, yours or someone else's — email safety@2night.co from the address on your account. Decisions are made by people, and we reverse our mistakes.

## How blocking works

Block from the same two places. A block is instant, silent and works both ways: you leave each other's Tonight feed, pings stop, a shared upcoming plan drops one of you, and the conversation leaves both inboxes. Nobody is notified. Every block is listed under Settings → Safety & privacy with an Unblock button, so a block is never something you have to email us to undo.

## Plans, calls and albums

Plans are public invitations. Give a real venue and a real time; a plan that names a private address or asks people to pay outside the App Store breaks rule four and will be removed. Hosts can remove a member from their plan; a plan that includes someone you have blocked simply shows as unavailable, and the app never says why.

Video calls are two minutes, peer-to-peer, and only ever between matched members. Recording a call, or a person, without consent breaks rule five. Private albums (a Gold and Platinum Black feature) can be viewed a limited number of times by the person you send them to; sharing someone's album further, or sending one to a person who did not ask for it, breaks rule five too — and rule two's ban on nudity applies inside albums exactly as it does on profiles.

## Under 18

The age selector starts at 18 and 2NIGHT does not verify age beyond what you declare, so we rely on you. If you believe an account belongs to a minor, report it with “fake or scam” and email safety@2night.co so it is looked at first. Accounts we believe to be underage are removed, and if a report describes a credible threat to someone's safety we pass it to law enforcement.

## How long reports are kept

Open reports are kept until decided. Reports closed without action are deleted after 90 days. For reports we acted on, the attached evidence is erased after 12 months and the report itself after 24, counted from the day we decided. If you delete your account, reports you filed are unlinked from you; reports about you stay on that schedule so nobody can wipe their record by re-registering.

## Community

See something serious? Email us — we read every message.

support@2night.co

TITLE: Guidelines — 2NIGHT
================================================================

Safety

# The rules, and what we do about them.

2NIGHT puts strangers in the same room on a few hours' notice. That only works if the rules are clear and somebody actually enforces them. Here are the rules, exactly how to report or block someone, and exactly what happens after you do.

## The rules

01
### Real people only
2NIGHT is for real people going out tonight. One account, and it's yours. No bots, no agencies, no accounts run on someone else's behalf.

02
### Be who you say you are
Your own photos, your own age, your own name. No impersonating anyone — not a celebrity, not a friend, not someone who doesn't exist.

03
### Respect. A pass is just a pass
No harassment, no hate, no threats, no pressure. If someone passes on you or stops replying, that's the whole answer. Take it and move on.

04
### 18 and over. No exceptions
2NIGHT is strictly for adults. If we believe an account belongs to someone under 18, we remove it. If you think a minor is on 2NIGHT, tell us immediately.

05
### Keep it clothed
No nudity and no sexually explicit content — not in your photos, not in your bio, not in a plan, and not sent to someone who didn't ask for it.

06
### Nothing for sale
No escorting or solicitation, no scams, no asking members for money, gifts or crypto. No spam, no promotion, no recruiting people to another app.

## What we check automatically

When you save your bio, we check it against a list of prohibited terms and refuse the save if it matches. It is a deliberately narrow tool: it catches the worst slurs and it will not catch anything clever.

We want to be straight with you about the limits of that. We do not scan the contents of your messages for abuse. There is a check on messages that looks for phone numbers, social handles and links — but that is a membership rule about when contact details can be exchanged, not a safety filter, and it never looks for abusive language. Nobody at 2NIGHT reads your chats.

Which is exactly why reporting matters. A word list cannot tell that someone made you uncomfortable. You can.

## How to report someone

Open their profile and tap the shield . You'll be asked to pick one of three reasons: inappropriate content , fake or scam , or harassment . That's the whole flow — pick one and it's sent.

You can also report from inside a conversation: the ⋯ menu at the top of a chat has Report in it.

Right now you report a person , not an individual message, plan or photo. If one specific thing is the problem, report the person and then email safety@2night.co saying which conversation or plan it was, so we know where to look.

## How to block someone

Blocking is in the same two places as reporting — their profile, and the ⋯ menu in a chat. When you report from a profile, we offer to block in the same step.

A block is instant, silent and works both ways. They are not notified and there is no announcement. From that moment you are gone from each other's Tonight feed, no ping from them reaches you, you drop off each other's plans, and the conversation leaves both inboxes.

If you were both going to the same upcoming plan, blocking takes one of you off the list — them, normally, or you if the plan was theirs. Past plans are left alone.

Blocking is reversible. Everyone you have blocked is listed in the app at Settings → Safety & privacy , each with an Unblock button. One tap and it's undone. Nobody has to email us to take a block back.

## What happens after you report

Your report lands in our safety queue the moment you send it, timestamped. The queue is ordered oldest open report first, it shows how long each one has been waiting, and it flags anything that has sat there longer than 24 hours.

We read that queue every day. We aim to act within 24 hours, and we always act within 72.

Acting means one of three things:

- We remove the account. It disappears from the Tonight feed, from likes, and from the plans list, and it can no longer message anyone, ping anyone, or post a plan. Its notifications are cut off and it is signed out.

- We warn it. The account stays, the person is told what has to stop, and the report stays on their record.

- We close the report. Sometimes nothing was broken. We would rather you over-report than sit on something, so a closed report is never held against the person who filed it.

If a report describes a credible threat to someone's safety, we will report it to law enforcement and give them what we hold.

## Reports are confidential

The person you report is never told who reported them. They do not see your name, and they do not see that a report exists at all until something happens to their account.

This is built into the database, not just promised here. No member can read a report — including the person who wrote it. You cannot pull up your own report after filing it, and neither can anyone else. That is on purpose: if you could read your own, someone who harasses several people could work out which of them filed. The safety queue is the only reader.

Blocking is just as quiet. Nobody is told they have been blocked.

## If you think we got it wrong

Email safety@2night.co from the address on your account and tell us what happened. Removals and warnings are decided by a person, and people make mistakes — if we made one, we reverse it and put your account back the way it was.

You can appeal a warning as well as a removal. There is no form and no deadline.

## How long we keep reports

A report is a record about two people, so we do not keep it forever:

- Still open, or being looked at — kept until it is decided. Nothing is ever deleted out from under an unfinished case.

- Closed with no action — deleted 90 days after we close it.

- Acted on — the evidence attached to it is erased after 12 months, and the report itself is deleted after 24 months. Both clocks start the day we decide, not the day you filed.

One routine in our database enforces every one of these periods. It runs automatically every night.

If you delete your 2NIGHT account, reports you filed are unlinked from you. Reports other people filed about you stay, on the schedule above — otherwise anyone could wipe their record by deleting and re-registering. There is more on this in our Privacy Policy .

## In an emergency, call for help first.

If you are in danger right now, contact your local emergency services before you contact us. We are one person reading a queue; they can reach you in minutes. Then tell us, so we can act on the account.

safety@2night.co

Meeting people

# How to Meet People Near You Tonight (Without Waiting for the Weekend)

By the 2NIGHT team
·
7 min read

It's 7pm. You're free, a little restless, and you don't want to spend another evening scrolling on the couch. The good news: meeting someone tonight is far more achievable than most people think — if you stop planning and start moving.

## Why “tonight” is the easiest plan to make

Most social plans die in a group chat. Someone says “we should hang out soon,” three people heart-react, and nothing happens. The problem isn't a lack of desire — it's distance in time.

Tonight has the opposite property. There's no calendar to negotiate, no “let me check my week,” no flaking three days later. The people who are free tonight are free right now, and that shared availability is the single most powerful ingredient in any plan.

## Step 1 — Decide what kind of night you actually want

Before you open any app or text anyone, get specific about the vibe. “I want to go out” is too vague to act on. Pick a lane:

- Low-key: a quiet drink, a coffee that runs late, a walk and a conversation.

- Social: live music, a busy bar, a games night, something with energy around you.

- Active: a late gym session, a run club, bouldering, a pickup game.

- Cultural: a gallery late-night, a film, an open mic, a pop-up.

Naming the vibe does two things: it makes you easy to match with, and it filters out plans you'd quietly resent.

## Step 2 — Set your radius (closer than you think)

The biggest mistake people make is casting too wide a net. A match across town who'd take 45 minutes to reach is, realistically, not happening tonight. Proximity is everything when the clock is running.

This is exactly the problem radius-based social discovery solves. Instead of browsing everyone everywhere, you set a distance — your street, your neighbourhood, your city — and only see people inside it. On 2NIGHT you choose how far the night reaches.

The Tonight Feed on 2NIGHT — real people near you, free right now.

## Step 3 — Lead with a plan, not a “hey”

Once you can see who's out, the difference between a dead conversation and a real plan is your opening message. “Hey” puts all the work on the other person and almost always stalls.

Don't ask someone to design the evening. Offer them an easy yes.
Compare these two openers. “Hey, how's your night going?” versus “There's live music at the place on the corner around 9 — I'm heading over, want to come?” The second one names a place, a time, and a low-pressure invitation.

- Reference something real — their status, a shared interest, the same neighbourhood.

- Suggest a concrete, public spot and a rough time.

- Keep it light — “no worries if not” lowers the stakes for everyone.

## Step 4 — Move fast, but meet smart

Momentum matters. The longer a “tonight” plan sits in a chat, the more likely it evaporates. Once you've agreed on something, lock the spot and the time and go. But moving fast doesn't mean abandoning common sense.

- Meet in a public, busy place — a bar, a café, a venue — never a private home on a first meet.

- Tell a friend where you're going and who you're meeting.

- Keep your own transport home, and trust your gut — if something feels off, leave.

We go deeper on this in our guide to going out solo and staying safe , which is worth a read before any first meet with someone new.

## Step 5 — Let one good night build the next

Here's the part people miss: a single good night isn't the goal — it's the seed. The person you grabbed a drink with tonight knows other people, other places, other plans. Meeting someone in person, tonight, is how a social life actually compounds.

So the next time it's 7pm and you feel that restless pull, don't put it in a calendar for “soon.” Soon never comes. Decide what you want, see who's near you, send the message that makes yes easy — and go.

## The short version

Pick a vibe, set a tight radius, open with a real plan instead of “hey,” meet somewhere public, and let one good night lead to the next. The whole thing can take fifteen minutes and change your entire evening.

## Stop planning. Start tonight.

2NIGHT shows you who's out near you, right now. Set your radius, match, and make a real plan — tonight, not tomorrow.

Download 2NIGHT

Dating apps vs. discovery

# Radius-Based Social Discovery vs. Traditional Dating Apps: Why “Tonight” Beats “Someday”

By the 2NIGHT team
·
8 min read

Both promise to help you meet someone. But a traditional dating app and a radius-based discovery app are built around completely different ideas of time — and that single difference shapes everything about how they feel to use.

## Two different models of meeting people

A traditional dating app is, at its core, a matchmaking queue. You build a profile, swipe through a deck of people who could be anywhere in a wide region, match, and then begin the slow work of a text conversation that might — eventually — become a date next week.

Radius-based social discovery flips the order. Instead of “who might I be compatible with someday,” it answers “who is near me and free right now.” The goal isn't a pen-pal — it's a plan in the next few hours.

## Where traditional dating apps win

Let's be fair: the swipe model exists for good reasons, and for some goals it's genuinely the better tool.

- Long-term intent: if you're looking for a serious relationship, the slower filtering of profiles, prompts and back-and-forth can help you find compatibility before you ever meet.

- Selectivity: detailed profiles let you screen for values, lifestyle and dealbreakers up front.

- Lower time pressure: you can match on Tuesday and meet in two weeks, which suits busy or far-apart schedules.

If your honest answer to “when do you want to meet?” is “sometime in the next month, with the right person,” a traditional app is a reasonable fit.

## Where radius-based discovery wins

But a huge share of the time, that's not the actual question. The real one is: “I'm free tonight — who else is, and where are they?” That's where proximity-first discovery pulls ahead.

- It respects your time: no months of texting toward a date that may never happen. You see who's out and you go.

- Shared availability is built in: everyone you see is free in the same window you are — the hardest part of any plan, solved by default.

- Distance is real, not abstract: a 5 km radius is a walkable plan; a match 50 km away you'll never meet isn't shown.

- It's not only dating: spontaneous discovery works for new friends, a plus-one to an event, or simply company for the evening.

Set your radius on 2NIGHT — from your street to the whole city.

## The “swipe fatigue” problem

There's a well-documented downside to the endless-deck model: it can start to feel like work. Hundreds of swipes, a handful of matches, most conversations fading after two messages. Psychologists call the underlying trap the paradox of choice — when options feel infinite, we commit to none of them.

When everyone is theoretically available someday, no one is actually available tonight.
Radius-based discovery sidesteps this by shrinking the field to something human-sized: not “everyone in a 100 km region, eventually,” but “these specific people, near me, out right now.” A smaller, time-bound set of options is far easier to act on.

## How 2NIGHT approaches it

2NIGHT is built around the tonight question. You set a one-line status — what you're up for this evening — and go live. You see the Tonight Feed of people near you who are also out, ping the ones you like, and match. From there it's a plan, not a pen-pal: a place, a time, and a real meet.

Your radius is yours to set. Keep it close at 5 km when you want somewhere walkable, open the whole city at 15 km, or go wide at 50 km when you're happy to travel for the right night. The philosophy never changes: proximity first, tonight first.

## So which should you use?

It's not really a war — it's a question of what you want this week. If you're patiently building toward a long-term relationship and don't mind a slow burn, a traditional dating app is a fine tool. If you're tired of conversations that go nowhere and you'd rather actually be out, in person, tonight, radius-based discovery is built for exactly that impulse.

The best nights rarely come from the most swiping. They come from deciding, at 7pm, that you'd like to meet someone — and then doing something about it. If that sounds like you, here's how to meet people near you tonight , step by step.

## In one line

Traditional dating apps optimise for “the right person, someday.” Radius-based discovery optimises for “real people, near me, tonight.” Pick the one that matches the night you actually want.

## Stop planning. Start tonight.

2NIGHT shows you who's out near you, right now. Set your radius, match, and make a real plan — tonight, not tomorrow.

Download 2NIGHT

New city · Safety

# Making Friends in a New City: A Guide to Going Out Solo (and Staying Safe)

By the 2NIGHT team
·
9 min read

Moving somewhere new is exciting for about a week. Then the boxes are unpacked, the novelty fades, and you realise you don't actually know anyone. Building a social circle from zero is one of the most underrated challenges of adult life — and one of the most doable, once you treat it as a skill rather than luck.

## Why making friends as an adult feels hard

As kids we made friends by proximity and repetition — the same classmates, every day, for years. Adult life strips both away. People are scattered, schedules are full, and the easy “we just kept running into each other” path disappears. Nothing's wrong with you; the structure that used to do the work is simply gone.

Which means the fix is structural too. To make friends in a new city you need to manufacture the two ingredients childhood handed you for free: proximity (being physically near the same people) and repetition (seeing them more than once).

## Go out solo — it's a feature, not a failure

Many people stay in simply because they have no one to go out with — and waiting for company is the single biggest reason newcomers stay isolated. But going out alone is quietly one of the best social tools you have. Without a friend to retreat into, you're far more approachable.

Make solo outings easy on yourself:

- Pick the bar, not the table: sitting at a bar or counter invites conversation in a way a corner table never will.

- Go where there's a shared activity: a class, a run club, a games night, a tasting — a built-in reason to talk to strangers.

- Become a regular: the same café or gym three times a week turns strangers into familiar faces, then into friends.

- Give yourself an exit: “I'll stay 45 minutes” removes the pressure and almost always turns into longer.

Join a plan near you on 2NIGHT — instant proximity, no waiting for company.

## Use proximity to your advantage

Here's where technology genuinely helps. The hardest part of a new city is that you don't yet know where your people are. Radius-based social discovery short-circuits that: instead of hoping to bump into the right crowd, you can see who's out near you tonight and what's happening close by.

This is exactly what 2NIGHT is built for. Land somewhere new, set your radius, and the local night is already in front of you — people who are out right now, plans you can join, company for the evening without needing a pre-existing circle.

## Turn one meeting into a circle

A social circle isn't built one friend at a time in isolation — it grows through connection. The person you meet tonight knows other people, hosts other plans, frequents other places. Your job is to convert single encounters into repeat ones.

One genuine evening, followed up on, is worth more than fifty introductions you never see again.

- Follow up within a day or two — a specific “that bar was great, let's do the Thursday quiz next week” beats a vague “we should hang out.”

- Say yes to the invitation behind the invitation — the house party, the friend's birthday, the group hike.

- Be the one who organises. People are grateful to whoever sends the “anyone free Friday?” message. Be that person.

## The going-out-solo safety checklist

Meeting new people is wonderful; doing it sensibly is non-negotiable, especially in a city you don't know well yet. None of this should make you anxious — treat it as the same kind of automatic habit as locking your door.

- Meet in public, busy places. A first meet is always a bar, café or venue — never a private home, never an isolated spot.

- Tell someone your plan. Share where you're going, who you're meeting and a rough timeline with a friend back home or new.

- Keep your own way home. Don't rely on someone you just met for your ride. Know your route and keep enough battery and cash.

- Mind your drink and your pace. Watch it being poured, keep it with you, and stay clear-headed enough to make good calls.

- Guard personal details early. Your exact address, workplace and routine can wait until trust is earned.

- Trust your gut. If anything feels off, you owe no one an explanation. Leaving early is always a complete sentence.

Remember that apps help you meet people but don't vet them — 2NIGHT doesn't run background or identity checks, so your own judgement is the real safety system. You can block and report anyone in a tap, but the habits above matter most. See our full Safety guidance for more.

## Give it time — and keep showing up

A real social circle in a new city usually takes a few months, not a few nights, and the people who build one fastest aren't the most charismatic — they're the ones who keep showing up. Every evening you go out is a small bet, and you only need a few to pay off.

So unpack the last box, pick a night, and go meet your city. The people you're looking for are already out there tonight — you just have to be out there too. If you're not sure where to start, here's how to meet people near you tonight .

## The takeaway

Friendship in a new city is proximity plus repetition, engineered on purpose. Go out solo, use your radius to find who's near, follow up relentlessly, and keep your safety habits automatic. Show up enough times and the circle builds itself.

## Stop planning. Start tonight.

2NIGHT shows you who's out near you, right now. Set your radius, match, and make a real plan — tonight, not tomorrow.

Download 2NIGHT

# Pages en français (French pages, added 2026-09-07)

## Qui sort ce soir près de vous ?
URL: https://2night.co/fr/

2NIGHT est une application de rencontre d'un soir pour iPhone qui vous montre qui sort près de vous ce soir, pour matcher et vous voir le soir même au lieu de discuter pendant des jours.

Vous êtes libre ce soir, vous avez envie de sortir, et votre groupe de discussion répond « un de ces quatre ». Les applications de rencontre classiques ne font pas mieux : elles vous montrent des profils qui seront peut-être disponibles une semaine sur deux. 2NIGHT répond à une seule question, et y répond ce soir : qui, dans un rayon que vous choisissez, est en ligne maintenant et veut sortir ?

Comment ça marche, en trois étapes

2NIGHT repose sur un rayon autour de votre position et sur un statut « Ce soir » qui expire à 5 h du matin ; votre profil n'apparaît dans le fil que tant que vous êtes en ligne, aux côtés des autres personnes qui sortent ce soir-là.

 Passez en ligne. Vous indiquez ce dont vous avez envie ce soir — un verre, un dîner, un rooftop, un concert, une expo, du sport, une balade, un café — et si vous êtes ouvert à une rencontre amoureuse, amicale, aux deux, ou au networking. Une ligne de texte facultative, et vous êtes visible jusqu'à 5 h du matin.

 Regardez qui sort. Le fil « Ce soir » n'affiche que les personnes en ligne à l'intérieur de votre rayon, avec une distance arrondie au kilomètre. Le compteur en haut de l'écran est le vrai chiffre renvoyé par le serveur, jamais une valeur inventée.

 Pingez, matchez, retrouvez-vous. Un ping réciproque ouvre une conversation qui reste active 48 heures : assez pour convenir d'un bar et d'une heure, pas assez pour devenir des correspondants. Un appel vidéo de deux minutes, d'iPhone à iPhone, permet de vérifier que la personne ressemble à ses photos avant de sortir.

Gratuit pour commencer

Rejoindre 2NIGHT et rencontrer des gens ne coûte rien. Le niveau Silver (gratuit) comprend un rayon jusqu'à 5 km, un quota de pings chaque soir et un Plan actif à la fois. Les abonnements Gold et Platinum Black élargissent le rayon (15 km, puis 50 km), retirent la limite de pings et ajoutent le Mode voyage, des Boosts, des Super Pings et la relance des conversations expirées. Tout est facturé par Apple et chaque prix est affiché dans l'application avant le moindre paiement : nous ne publions aucun tarif sur ce site pour ne jamais contredire votre boutique.

Ce que 2NIGHT est — et n'est pas

 Une application de rencontre pour ce soir, pas un catalogue permanent. Sans statut, vous êtes invisible ; une fois le statut expiré, vous disparaissez du fil.

 Une application qui respecte votre position. Les autres membres reçoivent une distance arrondie, jamais vos coordonnées. Aucun SDK publicitaire ni d'analyse dans l'application, aucune donnée vendue.

 Une application sans vérification d'identité. Il n'y a ni badge « vérifié », ni contrôle des antécédents. Les signalements sont lus par une personne, en général sous 24 heures et toujours sous 72 ; un blocage est immédiat, silencieux et réciproque. Votre jugement reste le vrai système de sécurité : rendez-vous dans un lieu public, prévenez un ami.

 Une application iPhone uniquement, réservée aux adultes de 18 ans et plus, qui ouvre ville par ville. Elle n'est pas encore sur l'App Store : la liste d'attente est le seul point d'entrée.

2NIGHT est une alternative à Tinder, Bumble, Happn et Pure pour celles et ceux qui veulent un rendez-vous spontané, le soir même. Si vous cherchez plutôt une relation longue avec des profils détaillés, une application classique reste un bon outil — nous le disons franchement dans notre comparatif 2026 des applications pour rencontrer des gens ce soir.
